summary: WhatsApp is Meta's free messaging and calling app, with end-to-end encrypted chats, voice and video calls, groups and status updates. The WhatsApp APK on WhatsApp's own download page is version 2.26.32.84, and it needs Android 6.0 or newer. It's free to use; the Play listing was updated October 31, 2026.
metaDescription: Download the official WhatsApp APK 2.26.32.84 for Android 6.0+ from WhatsApp's own source. Install steps, what's new, privacy notes and WhatsApp Web FAQ.

faq.q: How do I install WhatsApp on Android?
faq.a: Open Google Play, search for WhatsApp and check the developer is WhatsApp LLC before tapping Install. It needs Android 6.0 or newer. It's free to install, and Play keeps it updated automatically. On phones without Google Play, WhatsApp offers an official APK at whatsapp.com/android, signed with the same key as the Play version.

faq.q: Is it safe to download the WhatsApp APK?
faq.a: Yes, if it comes from WhatsApp itself. WhatsApp offers an official APK at whatsapp.com/android for phones without Google Play, signed with the same key as the Play version. Don't install WhatsApp APKs from other sites, and never use modified versions of WhatsApp, which WhatsApp bans and which can expose your messages.

faq.q: What is the difference between WhatsApp and WhatsApp Web?
faq.a: WhatsApp is the phone app where your account lives. WhatsApp Web is a way to use that same account in a computer's browser at web.whatsapp.com: you link it by scanning a QR code with the phone app under Linked devices. It isn't a separate download for your phone.

faq.q: What Android version does WhatsApp need?
faq.a: WhatsApp's download page lists Android 6.0 or newer as the minimum for the current version. On older Android versions WhatsApp stops working and asks you to update your phone. If you're close to the limit, check the requirement on whatsapp.com before relying on an old device.

Not in your chats. Meta announced in June 2025 that it would start showing ads in the Updates tab, where Status and Channels live, while personal chats, calls and groups stay ad-free. That's why our info table doesn't give a simple yes or no for ads.

Yes. Personal messages and calls on WhatsApp are end-to-end encrypted by default, so not even WhatsApp can read them. Chat backups to Google Drive aren't protected that way unless you turn on end-to-end encrypted backup under Settings, Chats, Chat backup.
